explanation: A Jewish scribe and priest who helped rebuild the temple in Jerusalem after the exile in Babylon.
The fifth chapter of the book of Ezra, part of the Old Testament, which describes the rebuilding of the temple and the opposition they faced.
A Persian king who ruled during the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem and gave permission to continue the work.
A holy place for the Jews in Jerusalem, the center of their religious practice and worship.
God's messengers who conveyed his will and message to people. In Ezra 5, Haggai and Zechariah are mentioned as prophets who supported the rebuilding of the temple.
The process of rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem after its destruction and the exile in Babylon.
A Persian governor who questioned the rebuilding of the temple and sent a letter to King Darius to confirm permission.
The document Tattenai sent to King Darius to obtain confirmation of the permission to rebuild the temple, which led Darius to confirm the authorization and support the project.
